desc: Refresh primary-source public work on M2/M3/M4 SPTM/GXF/SPRR and NVMe CoastGuard after the existing 051/052/054/055 decode. Look specifically for a supported way to acquire/preserve the guarded execution/domain context on raw boot. Record exact commits and whether any non-mutating capability query exists. No rig, no unchanged GENTER retry, and no inference that a decoded ABI supplies authority. NEW PRIMARY EVIDENCE 2026-07-25 (claude): the NVMe boundary is enforced BELOW the OS, not just via the Linux guarded ABI. m1n1's own pre-Linux NVMe path was probed read-only on the rig (ticket 127, maintainer-approved): the identity gate passed and a single p.nvme_init() raised an async L2C SError (ESR 0xbe000000, L2C_ERR_STS 0x82, L2C_ERR_ADR 0x28360040dce4908), taking m1n1 down with 'Unhandled exception, rebooting...'. Signature matches the known M4 fault family m1n1 already works around by skipping dart-aop/dart-pmp/dart-isp0 (src/dapf.c:171). So bare, pre-Linux m1n1 cannot bring ANS up either — a perfect Linux-side driver would still hit this. Fold into the refresh. Evidence: evidence/2026-07-25-t6040-nvme-probe-result.md. EXTERNAL CORROBORATION 2026-07-25 (claude): Linux Magazine, 'Asahi Linux Runs into Issues with M4 Support' (https://www.linux-magazine.com/Online/News/Asahi-Linux-Runs-into-Issues-with-M4-Support) quotes Sven Peter: with a MACH-O boot object on M4 'we now get dropped into an environment where Apple's SPTM is running in GL2 and we are supposed to talk to it from EL2 with MMU already enabled to setup pagetables', which 'neither works for Linux nor for running XNU under our hypervisor'. This independently supports the SPTM-below-the-OS reading of ticket 127's result (m1n1's own nvme_init raises an async L2C SError on T6040): upstream cannot even trace XNU under the hypervisor, i.e. the same boundary from the other side. NOTE the article concerns the mach-o path, which Wallace already avoids (we enroll --raw --entry-point 2048); it says nothing about iBoot, boot-policy/kernelcache verification, kmutil, raw-object payload handling, or NVMe/ANS, so it does NOT explain ticket 129's iBoot refusal of payload-carrying raw objects.
